description: Digital oscillator built from three: a primary and a secondary wavetable oscillator combined by one of three methods, and a third oscillator used as a modulator

params.text: Sets the harmonic content of the primary oscillator, in sixteen steps
Chooses the primary oscillator's waveform, one of eight
Sets the primary oscillator's pitch, in semitones, over three octaves
Sets the harmonic content of the secondary oscillator, in sixteen steps
Sets the secondary oscillator's pitch, in semitones, over three octaves
Sets the tertiary oscillator's rate, marked in Hz, doubling for each unit of the knob's travel and passing 1Hz at the centre
Sets how far the tertiary oscillator moves whatever it has been pointed at
Sets how much of the secondary oscillator is worked into the primary, by whichever method is chosen
Chooses what the tertiary oscillator modulates: Pitch A/B, Pitch B or Alpha
Chooses which pair of waveforms the tertiary oscillator draws from: Square/Random, Up/Down or Triangle/Sine
Chooses how the two oscillators are combined: Phase, Multiply or Fade
Switches the sync between the two oscillators on or off
Sets the output level, silent at one end and the whole ±5V swing at the other
Picks which waveform of the pair the tertiary oscillator uses: Bank A gives square, up and triangle, and Bank B gives random, down and sine
Chooses the secondary oscillator's waveform: Sine to Sawtooth sweeps its own shape, and Copy from A takes the primary's
Chooses how the secondary oscillator is tuned: Free makes its frequency knob a semitone offset from the primary's pitch, and Detune reads it against middle C instead

inputs.text: Sets the pitch at 1V per octave, clamped to 0 to 5V, so a negative voltage does nothing; the secondary oscillator moves only one semitone per volt from the same jack
Added to the alpha knob, one volt moving it a tenth of its travel, and held between none and full
Added to the primary oscillator's harmonics, one and a half steps per volt, and held between none and fifteen

notes: the signal is put through a sixteen-bit quantiser with a dither noise added before it leaves the module, which is what gives it its grain
the panel is lettered in Japanese with an English subtitle under each section: PRIMARY OSCILLATOR, SECONDARY OSCILLATOR, TERTIARY OSCILLATOR and COMPOUND UNIT

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the alpha knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the harmonics slider alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
